lessons.title: Azure Global Infrastructure: Regions & Availability Zones

slots.practicalActivity: Sign in to the Azure Portal (or create a free Azure account) and open the Regions page; find your nearest Azure region, note whether it has Availability Zones, then open 'Create a resource' and search for 3 real services (e.g. Virtual Machines, App Service, Azure SQL Database) and classify each as IaaS, PaaS, or SaaS.
slots.deliverable: A short note naming your nearest Azure region and its Availability Zone support, plus a 3-row IaaS/PaaS/SaaS classification table for 3 real services with a one-sentence justification each.

slots.practicalActivity: Take a guided tour of your own Azure Portal: open the Subscriptions blade and record your subscription ID and offer type, then create a resource group named rg-az900-practice in your nearest region and apply a tag Environment=Training to it.
slots.deliverable: A created resource group named rg-az900-practice tagged Environment=Training, plus your subscription ID and offer type recorded in a short note.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter review for Cloud & Azure Concepts: without looking back at the lessons, write a one-paragraph definition of cloud computing in your own words, sketch the IaaS/PaaS/SaaS responsibility split as a table, and confirm in the Portal that you can locate your subscription, your rg-az900-practice resource group, and your nearest region's Availability Zone info unaided.
slots.deliverable: A one-paragraph cloud-computing definition, an IaaS/PaaS/SaaS responsibility table, and a note confirming you located your subscription, resource group, and region/AZ info without referring back to the lessons.

lessons.title: Azure Compute Overview: VMs & App Service

slots.practicalActivity: Inside rg-az900-practice, deploy a small storage account (Standard_LRS) through the Portal, then deploy a virtual network with one subnet in the same resource group and region; open each resource's Overview page to confirm both live inside rg-az900-practice.
slots.deliverable: A deployed storage account and virtual network/subnet, both inside rg-az900-practice, confirmed via each resource's Overview page.

slots.practicalActivity: Open Microsoft Entra ID and view the Users blade for your directory, noting how many users exist and what role you have; then open Azure Monitor, select the storage account you deployed, and chart its 'Used capacity' metric over the last 24 hours under Metrics.
slots.deliverable: A written note on what you found in Entra ID's Users blade, plus a screenshot or description of an Azure Monitor metrics chart for your storage account.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending practice for Core Azure Services: for each of compute, storage, networking, identity, and monitoring, name the one real Azure resource or blade you deployed or inspected this chapter and explain in one sentence what problem it solves, then confirm all the resources you created still live under rg-az900-practice.
slots.deliverable: A 5-row table (Compute/Storage/Networking/Identity/Monitoring) naming the specific service used for each and what it solves, plus confirmation all resources are grouped under rg-az900-practice.

slots.practicalActivity: On rg-az900-practice, open Access control (IAM), review the Role assignments tab, and add yourself (or a test account) with the Reader role at the resource-group scope; then open the Azure Pricing Calculator and build a monthly cost estimate for the storage account and virtual network you deployed in Chapter 2.
slots.deliverable: A confirmed Reader role assignment on rg-az900-practice, plus a saved Pricing Calculator estimate showing the monthly cost of your Chapter 2 resources.

slots.practicalActivity: Add a second tag (CostCenter=Training) to rg-az900-practice, then in Azure Policy's built-in definitions search for 'Require a tag on resource groups' and open its JSON to see exactly what it checks; separately, look up one real compliance certification Azure holds for your region (e.g. via the Microsoft Trust Center) and note which one applies.
slots.deliverable: A resource group with two tags applied, written notes on what the built-in tag-requirement policy's JSON checks, and one named real compliance certification relevant to your region.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter review for Security, Pricing & Governance: write a short governance plan (5-8 sentences) for a hypothetical company with 3 resource groups, specifying which tags you'd require, who gets Owner vs. Reader access, and what budget alert thresholds you'd set in Cost Management.
slots.deliverable: A written governance plan covering required tags, RBAC role assignments, and Cost Management budget alert thresholds for a hypothetical 3-resource-group subscription.

slots.practicalActivity: Open Azure Cloud Shell (or install the Azure CLI locally), run az login and az account show to confirm your subscription, then run az group list --output table to list your resource groups from the command line; next, open rg-az900-practice in the Portal and use Export template to download its ARM template JSON, identifying the resources and tags sections inside it.
slots.deliverable: A Cloud Shell/CLI session showing az group list output, plus a saved exported ARM template JSON with the resources and tags sections identified in a written note.

slots.practicalActivity: Deploy a second storage account into rg-az900-practice twice: once through the Portal, once via az storage account create from the CLI, confirming both succeed and appear side by side; then review the AZ-900 exam's published skills-measured outline (Cloud Concepts / Azure Architecture & Services / Management & Governance) and identify your single weakest domain.
slots.deliverable: Two successfully deployed storage accounts in rg-az900-practice (one via Portal, one via CLI), plus a one-paragraph self-assessment naming your weakest AZ-900 exam domain.

slots.practicalActivity: Final course lab: delete rg-az900-practice entirely (az group delete --name rg-az900-practice --yes, or the Portal's Delete resource group button) to confirm everything you deployed this course is torn down and billing stops; then take a free official AZ-900 practice assessment (Microsoft Learn), score yourself, and map your 2 weakest questions back to the chapter of this course that covered them.
slots.deliverable: Confirmation that rg-az900-practice and everything inside it was deleted, plus an AZ-900 practice-assessment score with your 2 weakest questions mapped to the covering chapter.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After this course, a student can explain core cloud and Azure concepts, navigate the Azure Portal and CLI, and deploy, tag, secure, and tear down basic Azure resources — the AZ-900-level foundation the Azure Database Administrator course builds on.
